body:
The Federal Reserve left its key interest rate unchanged Wednesday despite persistently high inflation and a spike in energy prices caused by the Iran war. The Fed’s rate-setting committee reached the 9-3 decision after two days of deliberations, marking the fifth straight meeting at which the benchmark rate was kept at around 3.6%. Three Fed officials dissented in favor of a rate increase, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh described the policy discussion to reporters as a “good family fight.” [...] Kevin Warsh held his second news conference as Federal Reserve Chair, offering no surprises on interest rates. Our committee decided to vote by a 9 to 3 vote to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3 and 1/2 to 3 and 3/4 percent. What it's been since the last cut in December 2025. Warsh noted the country is straddling a resilient labor market and inflation that briefly surged to a 3-year high in May before retreating in June as the war with Iran continues to drive up energy [...] # Fed leaves interest rate unchanged but with 3 dissents as Warsh praises 'good family fight'
